Abstract. On a generic metric measured space, we introduce a notion of improved
concentration of measure that takes into account the parallel enlargement of k distinct
sets. We show that the k-th eigenvalues of the metric Laplacian gives exponential
improved concentration with k sets. On compact Riemannian manifolds, this allows
us to recover estimates on the eigenvalues of the Laplace-Beltrami operator in the
spirit of an inequality of [11].

# The second eigenfunction of the p$p$-Laplacian on the disk is not radial

In honor of Professor V. Lakshmikantham

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.na.2011.06.012Get rights and content

## Abstract

In this paper, we prove that the second eigenfunction of the p$p$-Laplacian, $p>1$, on the disk is not radial. Our proof is a combination of asymptotic analysis for $p\to +\infty $ and the application of interval arithmetic.

## Introduction

Let $D\subset {\mathbb{R}}^{2}$ be the open unit disk centered at the origin. We consider the following eigenvalue problem \{\begin{array}{cc}-{\Delta }_{p}u=\lambda {\left|u\right|}^{p-2}u\hfill & \text{in }D\text{,}\hfill \\ u=0\hfill & \text{on }\partial D\text{,}\hfill \end{array}$\{\begin{array}{cc}-{\Delta }_{p}u=\lambda {\left|u\right|}^{p-2}u\hfill & \text{in }D\text{,}\hfill \\ u=0\hfill & \text{on }\partial D\text{,}\hfill \end{array}$ where ${\Delta }_{p}u\stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=}\mathrm{div}\left({\left|\nabla u\right|}^{p-2}\nabla u\right)$ is the p$p$-Laplacian, $p>1$, and \lambda $\lambda $ is the spectral parameter. Note that the structure of the set of all eigenvalues of the p$p$-Laplacian ($p\ne 2$) beyond {\lambda }_{2}${\lambda }_{2}$ seems to be an interesting open problem.

The main result of this paper is the following.

Theorem 1

An eigenfunction associated with {\lambda }_{2}${\lambda }_{2}$ is not radial for all $p\in (1,+\infty )$.

For the case $p=2$, this fact follows from Payne [5] and the Fourier method for the Laplacian on a disk. In this paper we present a different argument to prove this fact and generalize it for arbitrary $p>1$. It is important to note that the result from Theorem 1 for p$p$ sufficiently close to 1 follows from Parini [6, Theorem 6.1]. The proof of Parini’s Theorem 6.1 is based on Cheeger’s inequality and implies that a second eigenfunction of (1) is not radial provided $1<p<{p}_{0}$, where {p}_{0}${p}_{0}$ is sufficiently close to 1. However, the value of {p}_{0}${p}_{0}$ is not quantified in [6].

This paper is organized as follows. In Section 2 we summarize some results which are a starting point for the idea of the proof of Theorem 1. This idea is explained in detail in Section 3. In Section 4 we quantify the constant {p}_{0}${p}_{0}$ from [6, Proof of Theorem 6.1]. Section 5 is devoted to a short overview of the interval arithmetic and an explanation of its role in the computer aided mathematical proofs. Based on this, the proof of Theorem 1 is given for p$p$ from a certain sufficiently large compact subinterval of (1,+\infty )$(1,+\infty )$. In Section 6 an asymptotic analysis with respect to $p\to +\infty $ is performed and Theorem 1 is proved for all p$p$ large enough (we again quantify how large). The proof of Theorem 1 then follows from combination of [6, Proof of Theorem 6.1] with Sections 4 Case, 5 Case, 6 Case. Appendix is a technical section where we describe how the algorithms presented in Section 5 can be implemented in Mathematica^{®}.

# On the nodal set conjecture for the $p$p-Laplacian in circularly symmetric domains

Published 1 Feb 2026 in math.AP and math.SP | (2602.01210v1)

Abstract: In 1990, Pütter shown that the nodal line of any second eigenfunction of the Dirichlet Laplacian on a planar bounded simply connected domain $Ω$Ω intersects the boundary $\partialΩ$∂Ω provided $Ω$Ω has the circular symmetry. By adopting the method of moving polarization, we establish similar information on the nodal set of second eigenfunctions of the Dirichlet $p$p-Laplacian on circularly symmetric domains in arbitrary higher dimension.

Authors (1)

  1. Vladimir Bobkov 

### Summary

  * The paper establishes the nodal set conjecture for circularly symmetric domains, showing that the nodal set of second eigenfunctions must touch the boundary.
  * Nodal sets are shown to touch the boundary across all dimensions and values of $p$ even in nonlinear $p$-Laplacian settings utilizing a moving polarization technique.
  * One of the assumptions employed to tackle the conjecture is the unique continuation of second $p$-Laplacian eigenfunctions.
